title: Time as a cue for human hunger
title_zh: 时间作为人类饥饿的提示
abstract: Many people eat at around the same times each day. This may result in meal times becoming predictive of eating's potential to be rewarding at that time (i.e., hunger). Time as a predictor of food reward has received much attention in animals but less in humans, even though many people organise eating around breakfast, lunch and dinner - words implying particular times of day. In this narrative review we examine if and how habitual meal times might cause hunger in people. We start by addressing a basic premise, can time-of-day predict food availability outside of modern clock-driven societies? We find it can, with moderate-to-strong evidence. We then turn to a harder question, is there evidence that habitual meal times can cause hunger? In animals, this focusses on the behavioral and physiological correlates of hunger, which provide positive weak-to-moderate and strong support, respectively. In humans, this means finding studies that control a key confound, namely people often eat after a period without food. This can generate other cues (e.g., an empty stomach) that may cause hunger, potentially resulting in cue competition. Currently, the human evidence is supportive, but weak. Finally, we evaluate models of how habitual meal times might cause hunger in animals, and then critically apply these to humans - noting that several key questions remain (i.e., cue competition). The implications for the human cephalic phase literature, the health impacts of regular/irregular eating patterns, how time may develop as a hunger cue and cause hunger, and its neural basis, are discussed.
abstract_zh: 许多人每天在大致相同的时间进食。这可能导致用餐时间成为预测该时间段进食可能带来奖励（即饥饿）的线索。时间作为食物奖励预测因子在动物研究中受到广泛关注，但在人类中关注度较低，尽管许多人围绕早餐、午餐和晚餐安排饮食——这些词暗示了特定的日间时间。在本综述中，我们探讨习惯性用餐时间是否以及如何导致人类饥饿。首先，我们讨论一个基本前提：在现代以时钟为驱动的社会之外，日间时间是否能预测食物可获得性？我们发现有中等到强有力的证据支持这一点。随后，我们转向更难的问题，即是否有证据表明习惯性用餐时间会导致饥饿？在动物研究中，这关注于饥饿的行为和生理相关性，分别提供了从弱到中等和强的支持。在人类研究中，这意味着需要找到控制关键混杂因素的研究，即人们往往在一段时间不进食后才进食。此过程可能产生其他线索（如空腹），这些线索可能导致饥饿，从而产生线索竞争。目前，人类证据支持这一观点，但证据较弱。最后，我们评估动物模型中习惯性用餐时间如何导致饥饿，并批判性地将其应用于人类——指出仍有若干关键问题（如线索竞争）。文中讨论了对人类头部相位（cephalic phase）文献的启示、规律/不规律饮食模式的健康影响、时间如何发展为饥饿提示并导致饥饿，以及其神经基础。
